accepts.because: a turn from the surface. The caller MUST promote the channel identity to context.channel, or every chat of the colony lands on the channel `default`; and it MUST promote the round to context.audience_set if the closed sessions of this talky are to reach a memory, because the generation this turn opens is where the round is recorded
an operator-forced session sweep outside the night timer
one tool result, coming back from a tool cell the parent wired
an advisor's answer, coming back from a second agent
a memory bundle, coming back from whatever keeps this agent's memory
a memory tool call the front model made, handed back in
a thread_recall tool call the front model made, handed back in: the collector serves it out of this turn's own round table, and without the lane every stub its curator leaves is a dead end
a prune verdict for the context window
a round that ran out of iterations, swept by an operator

emits.because: the finished turn, for the reply sink. Two sorts travel here and hop.round_capped tells them apart: a real answer and a round that hit max_iter. Since collector@2.1.1 a THIRD sort travels here and it is told apart by `hop.degraded`, not by `round_capped` (which such a message does not carry): a turn that could not be assembled at all because the store refused a read or a write (GH #343). `hop.store_error` carries the store's `error_code`, `hop.store_operation` the op it refused, and the text names both. A parent that renders an answer must branch on `degraded` -- without it a failure reads as a real reply
a closed session as one write batch, for wherever a day belongs. It carries context.channel and context.audience_set of the conversation -- off the generation row, not off the sweep that ended it

ONE finished turn per message after every stored turn and every stored answer -- never a batch (GH #298, ruling Q11): one user/assistant turn in messages[], hop.turn_id '<session_id>#<index>', hop.turn_index and hop.happened_at beside it, which is the shape a memory hive's episode lane reads. An occasion may carry several messages, one per turn not yet written. On unless the instance switches the collector's turn_write knob off

the sidecar a turn's answer carried, in the inline contract form; route it to the memory hive's in_remember door. ONE message per annotated turn, the raw block the model wrote as the text of a single turn -- never repaired, never re-serialised. Since talky@4.1.0 this is how per-turn extraction travels: it is NOT a tool call any more, so a parent that wired the old `hop.tool_name == 'remember'` lane rewires it to this route. It is a lane and not an obligation: without the extraction contract in the brain's instructions there is no block to cut and nothing ever travels here
a memory read this turn needs
a tool call for a cell the parent wired; hop.tool_name says which one

the report of a window prune: one message per cut session (hop.pruned_turns, hop.pruned_rounds, hop.prune_boundary), or a single zero report saying nothing was eligible. Since collector@2.1.1 a zero report can also mean the store REFUSED one of the prune chain's own reads or deletes: such a report carries hop.degraded together with hop.store_error and hop.store_operation, and a zero that was measured must not be read as a zero that was refused (GH #343). Every in_prune produces exactly one -- a caller that sends the lane MUST take it, which is why required_drains pairs the two
a normalised failure report. The parent MUST wire it -- unwired it dead-letters, loudly

required_drains.because: a prune answers unconditionally -- with what it cut, or with a zero report saying nothing was eligible. Undrained, every operator prune dead-letters its own answer and the deletions run unwitnessed: the cut happened, nobody can say what fell. Drain it with a PLAIN `hop.route == 'prune'` edge

edges.condition: has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'in_tool' || hop.route == 'in_advice' || hop.route == 'in_bundle' || hop.route == 'in_memory_call' || hop.route == 'in_thread_call' || hop.route == 'in_prune' || hop.route == 'in_round_sweep')

description.purpose: Scope marker of the talky composite: bundles the session keeper, the context collector, the brain, the tool dispatcher and the session summarizer behind ONE ingress, ONE reply exit, ONE write exit and ONE error drain. Everything the Egon rollout wired by hand -- the stamp, the seam, the dispatcher lanes, the loopback with restore_ttl, the close path, the handover -- is an internal edge here.
description.use_when: One per conversational agent. Instantiate it in the same mutation that wires the four ports plus the per-instance tool lanes; the composite is an island until an edge crosses into it.
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells (they are wired per instance on hop.tool_name), no memory hive, no surface proxy, no drain cell. The brain's identity, instructions and tool schemas live in its own cell.db -- the composite carries the topology, never the persona.
